title: Chapter 61 — Stubb Kills a Whale
paragraphs: If to Starbuck the apparition of the Squid was a thing of omens, to Queequeg it was quite a different matter.
"When you see squid," said the harpooner, sharpening his harpoon in the bow of his hoisted boat, "then you quick see sperm whale."

The next day was exceedingly still and sultry, and with nothing special to occupy them, the Pequod's crew could hardly resist the drowsiness brought on by such an empty sea. For this part of the Indian Ocean through which we were then voyaging is not what whalemen call a lively ground — meaning it offers fewer sights of porpoises, dolphins, flying fish, and other lively creatures that keep you awake in more active waters.

It was my turn to stand at the foremast-head. With my shoulders leaning against the slackened rigging, I swayed idly back and forth in what seemed enchanted air. No willpower could resist it. In that dreamy mood, losing all awareness, at last my soul went out of my body, though my body still continued to sway like a pendulum long after the power that first set it in motion has been withdrawn.

Before sleep entirely took me, I had noticed that the seamen at the main and mizzen mastheads were already drowsy. So at last all three of us hung lifelessly from the spars, and for every swing we made there was a nod from below from the slumbering helmsman. The waves, too, nodded their lazy crests. And across the wide trance of the sea, the vast trade-wind kept on blowing — but so drowsily that it seemed to breathe through a dream.

Suddenly bubbles seemed to burst beneath my closed eyes. My hands gripped the rigging like vises. Some invisible, gracious force preserved me — with a shock I came back to life. And there, close under our lee, not forty fathoms off, a gigantic Sperm Whale lay rolling in the water like the capsized hull of a frigate, his broad, glossy back of an Ethiopian sheen glistening in the sun's rays like a mirror. Lazily drifting in the gentle swell, the whale's vast mild head lay dripping with the sparkling spray. At intervals, his jets would rise into the still air. The few gentle clouds aloft seemed like lazy cotton bales tossed up for the breeze to carry.
"Clear away the boats! Luff!" cried Ahab. And obeying his own order, he slammed the helm down before the helmsman could reach the spokes.

The sudden shouts of the crew must have alarmed the whale. Before the boats were down, he majestically turned and swam away to leeward, but with such steady tranquility, making so few ripples as he swam, that thinking he might not yet be alarmed after all, Ahab gave orders that not an oar should be used and no man must speak above a whisper. So, seated like Ontario Indians on the gunwales of the boats, we silently sailed along, using only paddles. At times the whale turned to look at us with one slow, suspicious glance, then went on swimming.

"There go flukes!" was the cry, an announcement immediately followed by Stubb producing his match and lighting his pipe, for now a break was granted. After the full interval of the whale's deep dive had passed, the whale rose again. Being now ahead of Stubb's boat and much nearer to it than to any of the others, Stubb counted on the honor of the kill. It was obvious that the whale had at last become aware of his pursuers.
Yes, a mighty change had come over the fish. Now fully alive to his danger, he was going "head out" — that part projecting angled up from the mad churning foam he was brewing.

It will be seen elsewhere what a very light substance the entire interior of the sperm whale's enormous head consists of. Though apparently the most massive, it is by far the most buoyant part of him. So he raises it in the air with ease, and always does so when going at full speed. Besides, such is the breadth of the upper part of his head, and such the tapering cutwater formation of the lower part, that by cutting through the water at great speed, his head is completely protected from the impact of the waves.

"Start her, start her, my men! Don't hurry yourselves — take plenty of time — but start her! Start her like thunderclaps, that's all," cried Stubb, sputtering out smoke as he spoke. "Start her, now! Give them the long and strong stroke, Tashtego. Start her, Tash, my boy — start her, all! But keep cool, keep cool — cucumbers is the word — easy, easy — only start her up like thunderclaps, that's all."

"Woo-hoo! Wa-hee!" screamed the Gay-Header in reply, raising some old war-whoop to the skies, as every oarsman in the straining boat involuntarily lurched forward with the one tremendous leading stroke the eager Indian gave.
But his wild screams were answered by others equally wild. "Kee-hee! Kee-hee!" yelled Daggoo, straining forward and backward on his seat like a pacing tiger in his cage.

"Ka-la! Koo-loo!" howled Queequeg, as if smacking his lips over a mouthful of grenadier's steak. And so with oars and yells the keels cut the sea. Meanwhile, Stubb retained his place in front, still encouraging his men to the chase, puffing smoke from his mouth the whole time. Like desperadoes they tugged and strained, until the welcome cry was heard — "Stand up, Tashtego! — give it to him!" The harpoon was hurled. "A hit, a hit!" The whale dove. Now for the rushing flight through the water! The line raced through the grooves, ran foul. Tashtego snatched his knife from its sheath, and cutting the live line near the wooden post, freed it. Then he replaced the line in the groove with fresh coils. The boat now flew through the churning water like a shark all fins.

"Wet the line! Wet the line!" cried Stubb to the tub oarsman — who, snatching off his hat, dashed seawater into it. More turns were taken, so that the line began holding fast. The boat now flew through the boiling water like a shark all fins. Stubb and Tashtego changed places — stern for bow — a staggering business in any unsteady craft.

It may here be noted that, partly to show the necessity of this act, in the old Dutch fishery a mop was used to splash the running line with water. In many other ships, a wooden bucket is set apart for that purpose. Your hat, however, is the most convenient.

From the vibrating line extending the entire length of the upper part of the boat, now tighter than a harpstring, you would have thought the craft had two keels — one cutting the water, the other the air — as the boat churned through both opposing elements at once. A continuous waterfall played at the bow. A ceaseless eddy swirled at the stern. And like a great helpless whale itself, the boat with its streaming oars drifted sidewise through the sea. A continuous cascade of spray broke over everything.

"Haul in — haul in!" cried Stubb to the bowsman! And facing the whale, all hands began pulling the boat up to him while the boat was still being towed. Soon drawing alongside his flank, Stubb firmly planted his knee in the clumsy cleat and darted lance after lance into the fleeing fish. At the word of command, the boat alternately backing off and pulling closer, Stubb delivered his thrusts from every position.

The red tide now poured from all sides of the monster like streams down a hill. His tormented body rolled not in brine but in blood, which bubbled and seethed for furlongs behind in their wake. The slanting sun playing on this crimson pond sent back its reflection into every face, so that they all glowed to each other like red men. And all the while, jet after jet of white smoke was spouting up and spiraling against the sun.

"Pull up — pull up!" he now cried to the bowsman, as the weakening whale slowed his thrashing. "Pull up! — close to!" And the boat drew alongside the fish's flank. Reaching far over the bow, Stubb slowly worked his long sharp lance deep into the fish, and kept it there, carefully twisting and probing, as if cautiously feeling for some gold watch that the whale had swallowed, and which he was afraid of breaking before he could hook it out. But that gold watch he sought was the innermost life of the whale. And now it was struck. For starting out of his agony, the whale threw himself in mad anguish, rolling over and over, sending the slanting sun-glance across the water, spouting thick dark blood in jets that only grew more frenzied.

And now, his fury subsiding, the whale once more rolled into view, surging from side to side, spasmodically expanding and contracting his blowhole with sharp, cracking, agonized gasps. At last, gush after gush of clotted red gore, as if it were the purple dregs of red wine, shot into the frightened air, and falling back again, ran dripping down his motionless flanks into the sea. His heart had burst.
"He's dead, Mr. Stubb," said Daggoo.
"Yes — both pipes smoked out!" And withdrawing his own pipe from his mouth, Stubb scattered the dead ashes over the water, and for a moment stood thoughtfully eyeing the vast corpse he had made.
